label: USG Funding Guidelines 2026–27
notice: Copied from USG's public Funding Department Guidelines (current as of October 21, 2026). TrojanOps is a student project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by USG.

source.title: Funding Department Guidelines
source.edits: Two typos corrected: a repeated “six academic weeks” in §1 and “Restaurant diners” in §5.

rules.title: Weekly application window
rules.quote: Funding applications will be open once a week on Wednesdays and close at 11:59 PM.
rules.example: A request finished on Thursday has to wait for the next Wednesday window.

rules.title: Lead time with an approved USC vendor
rules.unit: academic weeks before the first payment is due
rules.quote: Applications must be submitted at least six academic weeks before the initial payment due date, for approved USC Vendors.
rules.example: If the caterer's first payment is due April 20, apply at least six academic weeks before that date.

rules.title: Lead time for travel
rules.unit: academic weeks before the first payment is due
rules.quote: Travel expenses must be made at least 9 academic weeks prior to the date of initial payment due date.
rules.example: Flights and a hotel for a conference need nine academic weeks; a request at six weeks is denied automatically.

rules.title: No events during breaks, study days or finals
rules.quote: USG Funding does not process applications or provide funding for events during University holidays, breaks, study days, or finals.
rules.example: A study-day social is not eligible, whatever its budget.

rules.title: Fixing an incomplete application
rules.quote: Incomplete applications will be returned to the applicant who must provide the necessary information within 2 business days.
rules.example: A missing vendor quote flagged on Monday must be sent by Wednesday, or the application is denied.

rules.title: Post Event Evaluation
rules.quote: All applicants must submit the Post Event Evaluation form found on the USG EngageSC page within three business days of the final day of the event.
rules.example: After a Friday event, the evaluation, with photos of members attending, is due Wednesday.

rules.title: Final invoices
rules.quote: Final invoices must be submitted no later than three business days after the final day of the event.
rules.example: Late invoices can cost the club its future funding.

rules.title: Annual maximum per club
rules.quote: Individual organizations may receive a maximum of $8,000 from the USG Funding Department per year.
rules.example: Startup Club's spring budget plans $6,200. Another $2,000 request would take it past $8,000.

rules.title: Funded events per semester
rules.quote: Each RSO can have up to 4 events funded per semester as long as it remains under $8,000 from the USG Funding Department per year.
rules.example: Startup Club's spring plan has three events, so it has room for one more.

rules.title: On-campus venue and personnel
rules.unit: USD for on-campus venue and personnel
rules.quote: The USG Funding Department will provide funding for up to $4,000 of the total cost associated with on-campus venue rentals and personnel.
rules.example: Startup Club's $1,500 for venue and audio-visual is within the $4,000 limit.

rules.title: Food per person
rules.quote: Food requests should not exceed a $35 per person maximum based on expected attendance, and raw food items requiring refrigeration or preparation are not eligible.
rules.example: Startup Club budgets $2,400 of catering for 60 expected Demo day guests: $40 a person, over the $35 limit.

rules.title: Lodging per night
rules.example: A $429-a-night conference hotel is over the limit. Every hotel request also needs a price comparison.

rules.title: Expenses USG does not fund
rules.quote: The following are not eligible for funding:
items: Durable goods (Items that are not for one-time use such as electronics, uniforms, etc.)
Raw food items requiring refrigeration and/or preparation
Rideshare costs (Uber, Lyft, Buses, Vans, Amtrak cabins, Car rentals, etc.)
Any refundable deposits and fees pertaining to cleaning/damage
Peer to Peer Payments (Airbnb, VRBO, PayPal, Zelle, CashApp, etc.)
On-campus events that are not open to all students
rules.example: Startup Club's "Speaker gifts and travel" line ($900) includes gifts, which USG does not fund.
rules.note: Any items critical to the function of the program may be considered as an exception to this rule at the board’s discretion.
